notes.meaning: Jesus continued his journey through Galilee, visiting cities and small villages to share the good news that God's kingdom had arrived. The twelve apostles traveled with him as his close followers and assistants. They helped announce his coming so people could hear him teach and see his works.

Several women who had been cured of physical sickness and freed from evil spirits also traveled with Jesus. Among them were Mary Magdalene, whom Jesus had rescued from seven demons, and Joanna, whose husband Chuza managed King Herod's palace affairs. In that culture, rabbis did not typically teach women disciples, yet these women freely used their own money and belongings to support Jesus and his disciples. Their generosity showed their deep gratitude for the healing and new life he had given them.

Crowds kept streaming out from nearby towns to find Jesus by the lake. To teach this vast gathering, Jesus spoke to them using a parable, which is a simple earthly story that illustrates a deeper spiritual truth. The story pictured a familiar farm scene that everyone in the crowd could picture easily.

A farmer went out to scatter his grain across a field. In that region, farmers usually threw the seed out first and then plowed the ground afterward. Some seeds landed on the hard walking path that cut through the field, where passersby stepped on them and wild birds quickly flew down and ate them up.

Other seeds landed on ground where a hard shelf of rock lay just under a thin layer of dirt. The shallow soil warmed up fast, causing the seeds to sprout quickly. As soon as the hot sun came out and the brief moisture dried up, the tender shoots withered away because their roots had nowhere deep to drink.

Some seeds fell into patches of soil that already contained the hidden roots of wild thorns and weeds. When the grain sprouted, the thorns shot up alongside it and grew faster. The weeds took all the sun and soil nutrients, choking the life out of the young plants before they could produce any grain.

Finally, some seeds landed in rich, healthy soil that had been cleared of weeds and rocks. These seeds took root, grew tall, and yielded an enormous harvest of one hundred times what had been planted. Jesus then called out loudly that anyone willing to listen should pay close attention to the spiritual lesson behind the story.

When Jesus was alone with his disciples, they asked him to explain what the farming story really meant. They sensed that it had a deeper message about God's kingdom, but they did not yet understand its lesson on their own.

Jesus told the disciples that God had granted them an understanding of the secrets of his kingdom, truths once hidden but now made clear through him. To the careless crowds, however, he spoke in parables so that Scripture was fulfilled: those who refused to believe would look without truly seeing and hear without understanding. The stories veiled the truth from people whose hearts were already hardened, while revealing it to those who sought him with humble hearts.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Luke softened the difficult language of Isaiah's warning compared to the earlier versions in Matthew and Mark to make the hard saying easier for his readers.

notes.meaning: Jesus explained the core meaning of the story to his followers. The farmer's seed stands for the word of God, which is the message of the gospel preached to human hearts. Just as real seed carries the power of new life inside it, God's message has the power to bring spiritual life to anyone who receives it.

The hard path represents people who hear the message of God carelessly or without interest. Before the truth can sink in, the devil snatches the message out of their minds so they will not put their trust in Jesus and be saved from sin. This shows how actively the enemy works to keep people in spiritual darkness.

The rocky ground represents people who hear the gospel and gladly accept it right away. However, because their commitment has no deep root, their faith remains only on the surface. When hard times, persecution, or testing arrive, their initial excitement fades and they walk away from Christ.

differ.view: Those with true saving faith can never completely fall away, so these hearers experienced only an emotional, surface response without true spiritual life.
These hearers possessed genuine faith for a time, but under severe pressure they stopped believing and abandoned their trust in Christ.

notes.meaning: The seed sown among thorns represents people who listen to God's word and start to grow. But as they go about daily life, their thoughts become crowded with the worries of life, the pursuit of money, and worldly pleasures. These distractions slowly choke out their spiritual life, so they never produce ripe, lasting fruit for God.

The good soil stands for people with honest, sincere hearts who hear God's word and hold tightly to it. They do not let trouble shake them or worldly pleasures distract them, but they patiently endure hardships over time. As a result, their steady trust produces a rich harvest of good works and godly character.

A person does not light an oil lamp only to cover it with a clay pot or hide it away under a bed. Instead, the owner sets it up high on a lampstand so that everyone who walks through the door can see the room clearly. In the same way, Jesus gave spiritual truth to his disciples not to keep it secret, but so they would shine that truth into the whole world.

Everything that is currently veiled will eventually be brought into full view, and every hidden secret will be uncovered. The truths of God's kingdom that Jesus was explaining privately to his disciples were meant to be declared openly to everyone later on. Nothing in human hearts or in God's plan can stay hidden forever.

Jesus warned his listeners to be very careful about the attitude with which they hear God's word. A person who values and uses the truth will receive even greater understanding from God. But whoever ignores the truth will end up losing even the little knowledge they thought they had.

Jesus' mother and brothers arrived at the place where he was teaching, hoping to speak with him. A thick crowd of people packed the room and surrounded the house, making it impossible for his family to push their way through to reach him.

differ.view: These brothers were younger children born to Joseph and Mary through their normal marriage after Jesus was born.

other.label: Catholic and Orthodox
other.view: Mary remained a virgin throughout her entire life, so these 'brothers' were either Joseph's sons from a previous marriage or close cousins of Jesus.

notes.meaning: Someone in the room passed the message along to Jesus, telling him that his mother and brothers were waiting outside asking to see him. This interrupted his teaching to see if he would leave the crowd to attend to his relatives.

Jesus responded by declaring that his true family consists of all who hear God's word and put it into practice. He was not dishonoring his earthly family, but showing that spiritual ties to God's kingdom are even deeper and more lasting than earthly bloodlines. Belonging to God's family comes through faithful obedience to his will.

Jesus told his disciples that they should sail across to the eastern side of the Sea of Galilee. They got into a boat together and set out across the open water. This journey took them away from Jewish towns toward a mostly Gentile area.

Tired from a long day of teaching, Jesus fell fast asleep in the back of the boat. A fierce windstorm suddenly rushed down from the surrounding hills onto the lake, churning up massive waves. The boat quickly began filling with water, putting all of them in extreme danger of sinking.

Panicking for their lives, the disciples rushed over and shook Jesus awake, crying out that they were about to drown. Jesus got up and directly commanded the howling wind and raging waves to stop. At his word, the storm ceased instantly, and complete calm settled over the water.

Jesus asked his disciples where their faith had gone, gently correcting them for giving in to fear while he was with them. Overcome with awe and terror, the disciples asked one another what kind of man this could be. By showing command over the winds and sea, Jesus demonstrated the very authority that the Old Testament says belongs to God alone.

The boat reached the eastern shore of the lake in the region of the Gerasenes, directly across from Galilee. This region was largely Gentile, populated by people who did not follow Jewish customs. Jesus went there intentionally to demonstrate his mercy and power in an unfamiliar territory.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Early Greek manuscripts vary between the names Gerasenes, Gadarenes, and Gergesenes, with Gergesa pointing to the actual lakeside village where the steep slope met the water.

notes.meaning: As soon as Jesus stepped onto the shore, a man controlled by demons came out to meet him. This man had suffered for a long time, refusing to wear clothes or live in a house, and instead made his home among burial caves outside the town. Burial sites were considered ceremonially unclean to Jews, but Jesus willingly stepped there to free a broken man from Satan's grip.

When the man saw Jesus, he dropped to his knees before him and screamed at the top of his voice. Speaking through the man, the demon addressed Jesus by his true title as the Son of the Most High God and pleaded not to be tortured. Even though the disciples had just wondered who Jesus was, the evil spirits recognized their divine Judge and trembled at his authority.
